survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a country note describing governance arrangements in Costa Rica’s adult skills system, not an analysis of student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC). As such, there is no sampling frame for students, no complex survey design, and no application of student-level weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife). The tables report administrative responsibilities and expenditure shares at subnational levels (e.g., % of general government expenditure at sub-national level), which are not estimated from survey microdata. Therefore, weighting guidance for PV/scaling is not applicable here; the note compiles governance information from OECD and partner sources.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are used in ILSA achievement testing (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC) to represent uncertainty in cognitive scores, but this OECD country note does not analyze student achievement outcomes. Instead, it synthesizes governance structures, stakeholder responsibilities, and expenditure shares for adult skills provision in Costa Rica. Missing-data handling is therefore not part of the methodology because no student-level dataset with item nonresponse is analyzed.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level analytic sample is constructed. The note uses compiled governance and administrative information for Costa Rica (including subnational expenditure shares and responsibility allocations) rather than microdata from an assessment.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note provides an overview of how Costa Rica’s adult skills system is governed across national, regional, and local levels. It describes a combined governance model in which national ministries and public institutions set strategies, manage funding, monitor labour market trends, and implement and deliver adult skills policies. The Ministry of Public Education oversees VET/HVET and adult education, while the National Learning Institute is the primary provider of VET/HVET and CET. The Ministry of Labour and Social Security develops adult education and ALMP/CET policies, with implementation supported by national employment agencies and local offices. Subnational actors (provinces, municipalities, and regional councils) mainly provide intelligence and localized implementation support, including municipal training offices and local branches of the Joint Institute for Social Aid. The note reports governance/expenditure structure (e.g., subnational expenditure share) and responsibility allocations by policy area rather than assessment performance metrics.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical large-scale assessment study and does not conduct ML prediction on student outcomes; it is a governance synthesis country note. Consequently, fields such as total_students, PV handling, missing-data handling, and ML techniques are not populated because there is no student microdata, no achievement scaling/PVs, and no predictive modeling pipeline. The extraction focuses on administrative responsibility mapping rather than statistical estimation.
